The build-order rail is explicit that the reader is the leaf and that a leaf blocking N rows is carved out, not buried.

THE DEFECT THIS ROW CLOSES. apps/daemon/src/http/goal-catalog-read.ts pins the GoalCreated payload to TWO exact key rosters and admits nothing else: LEGACY_GOAL_CREATED_KEYS (eight: budgetAccountRef, commandId, goalId, kind, planningRunRef, projectId, version, witness) and BRIEF_GOAL_CREATED_KEYS (nine: brief + the legacy eight). `exact()` is a LENGTH equality plus a total hasOwn check, so a TENTH key fails both rosters and goalEntry returns refused("GOAL_CATALOG_READ_MALFORMED"). THE SHAPE. Add a THIRD exact roster of TEN keys — the brief nine plus the bound source reference — in the same additive style the file already uses for LEGACY -> BRIEF, and keep the hybrid refusal for everything else. The reader defines the admitted shape and fc42ae5e's writer conforms to it; that ordering is deliberate, because a writer that ships first takes the catalog down. The file's own docstring at :28-29 currently asserts a ten-key row is "a HYBRID no writer can produce" — that sentence becomes FALSE when fc42ae5e lands and must be rewritten in the same commit, not left to contradict the code.

THE KEY NAME IS THIS ROW'S TO FIX, and fc42ae5e adopts it verbatim: coordinate the exact literal with that row before landing, record it in a comment, and @mention its seat. Do not invent a second spelling.

ORDERING IS A SAFETY CONSTRAINT, NOT PAPERWORK. Phase 3 — RED FIRST, with a DIVERGENCE FIXTURE TRIO, in apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-goal-catalog.test.ts only. Epic rail 7(A) binds here: two mechanisms refuse with an identical code at an identical layer, so a single 'reaching' fixture that trips both proves the system refuses, not that a given guard refuses — and loosening one fence alone would leave the suite green. Construct three arms that each isolate exactly one mechanism, and say in each arm's title and a comment which fence is the ONLY one that can refuse it. ARM A (kind-only): a `goal.create_with_source` decision trace carrying the ORDINARY nine-key BRIEF payload — fence B cannot refuse it, so only fence A can. ARM B (roster-only): a `goal.create` trace carrying the TEN-key source-bearing payload — fence A cannot refuse it, so only fence B can. ARM C (the real shape): a `goal.create_with_source` trace with the ten-key payload, which must READ BACK with the goal visible, the brief intact and the agreed source reference exposed on the entry. Every arm asserts the exact tuple {code: "GOAL_CATALOG_READ_MALFORMED", layer: "GOAL_CATALOG_READ", outcome: "REFUSED"} — the reason code AND the refusing layer, never merely that it refused. Run the three arms and quote the RED output with its nonzero executed count before writing any production byte. If ARM A or ARM B comes back GREEN, that is a FINDING to report in a comment, not a pass: it means the fence you think you are isolating is not the one refusing.

Phase 4 — GREEN, minimum implementation, in apps/daemon/src/http/goal-catalog-read.ts only. Widen BOTH fences and nothing else. (1) Fence A: admit `goal.create_with_source` alongside `goal.create` in the command-kind gate; leave `event.aggregateSequence !== 1` untouched, since the new kind still writes GoalCreated at sequence 1. Prefer a frozen two-member constant over an inline `||` so the admitted set is enumerable by the roster test. (2) Fence B: add a THIRD frozen roster of TEN keys — the agreed source key plus the BRIEF nine — declared in the same additive style the file already uses for LEGACY -> BRIEF, and select it with the same `exact()` helper. DO NOT loosen `exact()` itself: turning its length equality into a subset check would admit every hybrid this file exists to refuse, and is the mutant step 5 drills for. (3) Expose the admitted source reference on `GoalCatalogEntry` as a nullable field — null for legacy and brief rows, the reference for source rows — and validate it with the same `nonEmptyRef` discipline the other refs get, refusing GOAL_CATALOG_READ_MALFORMED when present but empty. (4) Rewrite the :28-29 docstring, which today asserts a ten-key row is "a HYBRID no writer can produce": describe THREE rosters and say which writer produces each. Keep the module's layer constant private. Re-run step 2's trio: ARM C greens, ARMs A and B green only because their fence was deliberately widened. Production file stays under the 250-line target; measure it.

Phase 3 (coverage) — BIDIRECTIONAL roster and blast-radius arms, in http-listener-goal-catalog.test.ts. (1) Both directions, per the standing roster rail: every admitted shape reads AND every non-admitted shape refuses. Enumerate the admitted set from the reader's OWN exported roster/kind constants, not from a hand-copied list in the test, and assert SET EQUALITY — a test that iterates only the roster constant shrinks with it and stays green while a shape silently vanishes. (2) Still-reads: an eight-key LEGACY row reads with brief null; a nine-key BRIEF row reads unchanged; the new ten-key SOURCE row reads with its reference exposed. Quote nonzero executed counts.

Phase 3 (negative controls) — MUTATION DRILLS, one at a time. Both owned files are TRACKED, so restore is proven by `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` in a call SEPARATE from the restore; do not rely on a bare 'the command returned'. D4 KEY-RENAME: rename the source key in the roster only -> the foreign-name refusal arm AND the valid-source arm both red, proving both are bound to ONE literal rather than to a test-local copy. D5 REF-VALIDATION: drop the nonEmptyRef check on the source reference -> the empty-reference refusal arm reds. A GREEN drill is a FINDING to report in a comment, never a pass to bank — report it and stop rather than proceeding.

Phase 5/6/7/8 — GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, DURABLE RECORD, PATHSPEC COMMIT. Disclose any foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and paths; if task-3f71ba30 has still not landed you will see its red on daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:151, which is NOT yours. ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, each answered with a measurement or an explicit N/A: duplicate keys across the three rosters; a payload whose tenth key is present but null, empty, oversized or the wrong type; a source row whose goalId or projectId disagrees with its trace; two source rows in one page; a source row at aggregateSequence != 1; interaction with the pagination cursor (does a source row page and resume correctly); and whether any refusal detail now leaks the source reference into a log or response body.
